plan_a_advantages: More targeted training for trail-specific skills like hill climbing.
Incorporates strength training for injury prevention and power.
Includes shorter, higher-intensity workouts to improve speed and power.
plan_b_advantages: Greater emphasis on aerobic base building, which is a foundational element of trail running.
Longer, continuous runs could be beneficial for building overall endurance, though this is less critical for a runner focused on speed.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates more targeted hill work and shorter, more intense interval sessions (hill repeats) which directly address the demands of trail running – climbing and maintaining speed on varied terrain. Plan B focuses heavily on aerobic endurance with longer, steady-state runs, which, while beneficial, doesn't provide the same stimulus for improving speed and power. Plan A’s inclusion of strength training is also a key advantage, crucial for trail runners to prevent injury and improve efficiency.
